purpose: Generate a bounded, fully programmatic 1024-pixel corpus that separates questions requiring one local high-resolution crop from questions answerable using a global view, before any router or responder training.
split_unit: scene family; base and answer-changing variants remain in the same split

read_local_digit.description: Identify a globally visible color-shape address, then read a small digit that is intended to be lost in the 1024-to-224 global resize but preserved by a source-resolution panel crop.

read_global_border.description: Read a prominent outer-border color without purchasing a crop.

required_before_training: all 640 rendered images have unique SHA256 values
manifest and audit-sheet hashes are recorded
all 48 frozen audit-sheet items are visually inspected for target identity, answer, counterfactual change, and crop legibility
a preprocessing-floor test confirms local digits are materially harder in the 224-pixel global view than in the oracle crop
sealed_test remains inaccessible to checkpoint, threshold, prompt, or architecture selection
a separate training protocol pins parent checkpoints, losses, baselines, budget, and stop rules
claim_boundary: This programmatic corpus can diagnose one bounded evidence-acquisition mechanism. Passing generation, visual audit, or a future model test cannot establish natural-image, document, GUI, or general multimodal capability. The STOP task is intentionally simple and must not be treated as a broad abstention benchmark.
